title: Missile strike hits Kramatorsk railway station during evacuation
body:
On 8 April 2022 a missile struck the railway station in Kramatorsk, in Ukraine's Donetsk Oblast, where civilians were waiting for evacuation trains from the Donbas as Russian forces prepared an offensive in the east. Pavlo Kyrylenko, head of the Donetsk Regional Military Administration, said in a Facebook post that a Russian Tochka-U missile had hit the station.

Kyrylenko reported that 50 people had died, including five children. Of these, 38 died at the station and 12 died in hospital. He said 98 people were hospitalised, including 16 children, 46 women and 36 men, and he warned that more injured people would likely need medical care in the following day or two, so the casualty count could rise. Kramatorsk mayor Oleksander Honcharenko estimated that about 4,000 people were at the station at the time of the attack.

Ukrainian officials initially said an Iskander missile had been used but later said it was a Tochka-U. By 10 April Kyrylenko reported that the death toll had risen to 57. Russia's Defence Ministry denied responsibility, calling the reports a provocation and saying it had not conducted or planned artillery fire in Kramatorsk on 8 April.
